Documented precedent: FAN-2541/FAN-2550/FAN-2551, and now every one of these 9 jobs.

Same blocking contract and exit codes as pixellab_generate_pack.py.

generation_params_common.frame_count_returned: 9 (8 animated + 1 stored reference frame, all kept — same convention as FAN-2542)
generation_params_common.note_frame_count_ceiling: PixelLab rejects frame_count>8 for a 256x256 object (422: 'frame_count 10 too high for 256x256 image. Maximum frame_count: 8').

prompt_lessons: A prompt phrased only as 'starts small and fades' can return frames whose visible-pixel count is fully transparent at the start/end (hammer/cast_flash, 1st attempt) or non-monotonic/out-of-order in brightness (axe/cast_flash, 1st attempt) — both regenerated with an explicit 'every single frame shows visible glowing light, never a fully empty or nearly-invisible frame' + 'smoothly and monotonically expands/shrinks' clause, which fixed both.

A rift/shockwave description that only asks for a 'hammer silhouette' embedded in a crater came back with the hammer barely readable under debris; asking explicitly for 'a big heavy war hammer head lying flat ... clearly readable bold silhouette at the center' produced a hammer head that reads clearly in every frame while only the radiating cracks pulse.

Overlong single-line descriptions (≈480 words) triggered an outright object creation failure (status: failed) once (hammer/rift_shockwave 2nd attempt with an even longer prompt); shortening to ≈380 characters fixed it — keep description/animation-description under roughly 400 characters each.
These parameters are the reference process for the assassin trio (FAN-3013→FAN-3014) and the remaining 46 scenes.
